questions.question: Water has the highest density at nearly ______ Kelvin.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 277.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water Density**

 
 
• The density of water is measured as weight per unit volume of the water and it is mainly **dependent on the temperature of water.**
 
• In the crystal lattice, there are lot of **void area** present, when the water is in its ice form doe to sufficient hydrogen bonding between the water molecules. This **crystal structure** begins to collapse as the ice begin to melt.
 
• As the **temperature increases**, the molecules of water start migrating farther from each other hydrogen bond start collapsing and therefore the molecules start coming close to each other resulting in **the increase of water density and decrease in volume**.
 
• At **273 kelvin (****0°C)**, ice clusters are seen in the water which are allowed to move freely. Due to the vacant spaces present in the ice clusters, **its density get reduced and volume is increased**.
 
• At 0 and 227 kelvin the temperature decreases and thus the density decreases.
 
• At **277 kelvin** (4°C), as the temperature increases the clusters begin to deform, resulting in the** highest water density**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The unit of temperature kelvin is converted into celcius (C) by 
 
 
• **K= C+273, thus 277 kelvin is 4°C ( K =4+273=277 kelvin)**
 
 
 
• **After 277 k**, the** rise in volume due to the expansion of liquid water becomes more** than the reduce in volume caused due to hydrogen bond breakage.
 
• After 277 k, there is a **net gain in volume during heating, which leads to a decrease in density**.
 
• It falls within a variety of **abnormal physical properties**.
 
• As compared to liquid water, the **density of ice is less and thus ice floats on water**. 
 
• When we freeze the water, the density of ice is reduced by about **9%**.

questions.question: The percentage change in demand for a good, divided by the percentage change in its price is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**price elasticity of demand.**__

**Given:**

The percentage change in demand for a good, divided by the percentage change in its price is known as price elasticity of demand.

**Concept used:**

Price elasticity of demand = (% change in Q)/(% change in P) 

**Calculations:**

Let the percentage change in demand for goods be Q, and

Let the percentage change in its price by P

According to the question,

⇒ { [ (Qf - Qᵢ)/( (Qf + Qᵢ)/2) ] ÷ [(Pf - Pᵢ)/( (Pᵢ + Pf)/2) ] } × 100

⇒ { [ (Qf - Qi)/( (Qf + Qi)/2) ] × 100 } ÷ { [(Pf - Pi)/( (Pi + Pf)/2) ] × 100 } 

⇒ (% change in Q) ÷ (% change in P) = Price elasticity of demand

**∴ The percentage change in demand for a good, divided by the percentage change in its price is known as the Price elasticity of demand.**

questions.question: A field is in the shape of a rhombus whose side is 122 m. The length of one of its diagonals is 240 m. What is the area (in m²) of the field?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **rhombus**, diagonals are **perpendicular bisectors** of each other.

Half of the given diagonal = 240 ÷ 2 = 120 m.

Using Pythagoras triplet for the side (122) and half-diagonal (120):

Other half-diagonal = √(122² − 120²) = √(2 × 242) = √484 = 22 m.

Second diagonal (d₂) = 2 × 22 = 44 m.

Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 240 × 44 = 120 × 44 = 5280 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 5280 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the **rhombus** (a) = 122 m

Length of one **diagonal** (d₁) = 240 m

**Formula Used:**

1) a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

2) Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c52ccbe6c73409defcb6cf6221983cf259fa402018b92c8ebfc0e1c7350dcddb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the other diagonal be d₂.

⇒ 122² = (240/2)² + (d₂/2)²

⇒ 14884 = 120² + (d₂/2)²

⇒ 14884 = 14400 + (d₂/2)²

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 14884 − 14400

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 484

⇒ d₂/2 = √484 = 22 m

⇒ d₂ = 22 × 2 = 44 m

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 240 × 44

⇒ Area = 120 × 44

⇒ Area = 5280 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 5280 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all sides equal. Its diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

Perimeter of Rhombus

Perimeter = 4 × side = 4a.

Relation between Side and Diagonals

4a² = d₁² + d₂², where a is the side and d₁, d₂ are diagonals.</p

• It has occasionally been referred to as **"regur,"** a word derived from the Telegu word** "Regada." **This soil is a product of the erosion of basalt from the Deccan Highlands.

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a job in 20 days. Q and R together can complete the same job in 30 days. P and R together can complete the same job in 30 days. What is the respective ratio of the number of days taken by P when completing the same job alone to the number of days taken by R when completing the same job alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P and Q together can complete the job in 20 days.

Q and R together can complete the job in 30 days.

P and R together can complete the job in 30 days.

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

One-day work of P and Q = 1/20 ...........(1)

One-day work of R and Q = 1/30 ...........(2) 

One-day work of P and R = 1/30 ...........(3)

Adding the equations (1), (2), and (3)

(P + Q) + (R + Q) + (P + R) = (1/20) + (1/30) + (1/30)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (1/20) + 2(1/30)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (1/20) + (1/15)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (3 + 4)/60

⇒ (P + Q + R) = 7/120

Total work done by all P, Q, and R in one day is 7/120

Now total work done by P alone in one day

⇒ (P + Q + R) - (R + Q) = (7/120) - (1/30)

⇒ P = (7 - 4)/120

⇒ P = 3/120 = 1/40

P alone can do the job in 40 days

Now total work done by R alone in one day

⇒ (P + Q + R) - (P + Q) = (7/120) - (1/20)

⇒ R = (7 - 6)/120

⇒ R = 1/120 

R alone can do the job in 120 days

Now the ratio of work done by P and R alone

⇒ P/R = 40/120 = 1/3 = 1:3

**∴ The ratio of work done by P and R alone is 1:3.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a solid cylinder is (2)/(3) of its total surface area. If the solid cylinder has a total surface area of 231 cm², then find the volume of the cylinder (in cm³). (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **CSA : TSA** = 2 : 3 ⇒ **h : (h + r)** = 2 : 3 ⇒ **h = 2r**.

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3 units = 231 cm² ⇒ 1 unit = 77 cm².

Area of two bases (2πr²) = TSA − CSA = 3 units − 2 units = 1 unit = 77 cm².

Radius r² = 77 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 49/4 ⇒ **r = 3.5 cm**.

**Volume** = CSA × (r/2) = (2 × 77) × (3.5 / 2) = 154 × 1.75 = 269.5 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 231 cm²

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = (2/3) × TSA

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bfc0b2dfd653d3f7ed069c50043255bc46d88de14c4830a7db1746c565204d9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA = (2/3) × 231 = 154 cm²

⇒ TSA = CSA + 2 × Area of base

⇒ 231 = 154 + 2πr²

⇒ 77 = 2 × (22/7) × r²

⇒ r² = (77 × 7) / (2 × 22) = (7 × 7) / 4 = 49 / 4

⇒ r = 7 / 2 = 3.5 cm

⇒ Now, CSA = 2πrh = 154

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × h = 154

⇒ 22 × h = 154

⇒ h = 154 / 22 = 7 cm

⇒ Volume = πr²h

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (3.5) × (3.5) × 7

⇒ Volume = 22 × 12.25 = 269.5 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Properties

For a cylinder with radius r and height h, Volume = πr²h, and the ratio of Volume to CSA is always r/2.

Total Surface Area

TSA includes the curved surface and the area of two circular ends: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr².

Hollow Cylinder

The volume of a hollow cylinder with external radius R and internal radius r is V = πh(R² − r²).</p

In the below question two statements I and II are given. These statements may be either independent causes or may be effects of independent causes or a common cause. One of these statements may be the effect of the other statements. Read both the statements and decide which of the following answer choice correctly depicts the relationship between these two statements.

**Statements:**

I) India's economy sees record growth during the deadly Covid second wave.

II) Manufacturing and Health sectors drove growth during the second lockdown.

options.text: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect.
Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect.
Both the statements I and II are independent causes.
Both the statements I and II are effects of independent causes and none can be a possible cause of the other.

questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Manufacturing and Health sectors drove growth during the second lockdown (Cause) and as the demand grew rapidly, India's economy sees record growth during the deadly Covid second wave (Effect)

Hence **Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ 

What are Causes?

Causes are the conditions under which an event occurs.

For example, can you guess the causes for the following? 

The police increased security around the President's house.

Lots of people buy a particularly expensive brand of washing machines around Diwali. Easily, we can guess the causes for the above events. 

There were reports of threats against the President. 

There was a high discount or sale for that brand during Diwali.

Sufficient & Necessary Conditions:

In a cause and effect question, the cause is the sufficient condition. It is assumed that the sufficient condition of the occurrence of the events must include the different necessary conditions as well. 

A necessary condition is one that must be satisfied for the occurrence of an event. 

E.g. You must adhere to the deadline to get your work appraised. 

This means if you get your work appraised, you have to adhere to the deadline. Or; if you do not adhere to the deadline, you do not get your work appraised. 

A condition is called a sufficient condition if in a certain event, you are satisfied with the results.

E.g. Being human is a sufficient condition for being a mammal. Being a human is not possible unless one is also a mammal. But it is not necessary that being human is a necessary condition for being a mammal.

questions.question: Δ RST is an obtuse isosceles triangle with m∠R = 16° and m( {overline {TR} } ) > m( {overline {ST} } ) . What is the measure of ∠S?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **isosceles triangle** ΔRST, two angles must be equal. Given **m∠R = 16°**.

Condition **TR > ST** implies angle opposite to TR must be greater than angle opposite to ST.

∴ **m∠S > m∠R**, so m∠S cannot be 16°.

If equal angles are m∠R = m∠T = 16°, then **m∠S = 180° − (16° + 16°) = 148°**.

Since 148° > 90°, it satisfies the **obtuse** condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 148°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔRST is **obtuse isosceles** triangle.

m∠R = 16°

m(TR) > m(ST)

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

Side-Angle Inequality: The side opposite to the **greater angle** is longer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/603b6e17d57ddf0a0e810ef8906cbddce54d0d7d4bd2ae3985b53f3ad26afe4c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔRST, the side **TR** is opposite to ∠S and side **ST** is opposite to ∠R.

⇒ Given TR > ST ⇒ **m∠S > m∠R**

⇒ Since m∠R = 16°, we must have m∠S > 16°.

⇒ For an **isosceles triangle**, two angles must be equal. Possible cases for (m∠R, m∠S, m∠T):

⇒ Case 1: If m∠S = m∠T, then 16° + 2 × m∠S = 180° ⇒ 2 × m∠S = 164° ⇒ m∠S = 82°. (Triangle is 16°, 82°, 82° which is **acute**, so rejected).

⇒ Case 2: If m∠R = m∠T = 16°, then m∠S = 180° − (16° + 16°) = 148°.

⇒ Here 148° > 16°, which satisfies the condition m∠S > m∠R (TR > ST).

⇒ Also, 148° > 90°, making the triangle **obtuse**.

**∴ The correct answer is 148°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle-Side Relationship

In any triangle, the side opposite to the largest angle is the longest side, and the angle opposite to the longest side is the largest angle.

Obtuse Isosceles Triangle

A triangle where one angle is greater than 90° and two sides (and their opposite angles) are equal. The equal angles must always be acute.

Sum of Angles Property

The interior angles of any Euclidean triangle always sum up to exactly 180°.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 9200 was lent partly at 5% p.a. and the rest at 8% p.a., both earning simple interest. Total interest received after 3 years was Rs. 1812. The sum (in Rs.) lent at 5% p.a. was
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principle (P) = Rs. 9200 

Rate of interest (R₁) = 5% per annum 

Rate of interest (R₂) = 8% per annum 

Time period (T) = 3 years 

Total interest received = Rs. 1812

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

Let the sum lent at a 5% rate be 'x', then the sum lent at 8% be (9200 - x)

⇒ SI = (SI at 5%) + (SI at 8%)

⇒ 1812 = [(x × 5 × 3)/100] + {[(9200 - x) × 8 × 3 ]/100}

⇒ 1812 = [15x/100] + {[220800 - 24x]/100}

⇒ 1812 = 15x + 220800 - 24x

⇒ 181200 = 220800 - 9x

⇒ x = (220800 - 181200)/9

⇒ x = 39600/9 = Rs. 4400

**∴ The sum (in Rs.) lent at 5% p.a. was Rs. 4400.**

questions.question: Rajat joined school on 26th February 2020, a Wednesday, and he has his examination scheduled on 26th May 2020. There was no holiday or leave, except Sundays. For how many active working days did he go to school before the exam?
questions.solution:
Number of days starting from 26th February 2020 to 26th May 2020 = February (4) + March (31) + April (30) + May (25) = 90 days** as 2020 is a leap year.**

26th February is held on Wednesday. So 26 February (Wednesday) + 4 = 1 March (Sunday)

Since it was Sunday on 1st March, every 7th day from 1st March will be a Sunday

Total number of Sundays from 26th February 2020 to 26th May 2020 = March (5) + April (4) + May (4) = 13 

Total number of working days = Total number of days - Total number of Sundays = 90 - 13 = 77

Therefore, there are** 77 active working days.**

**Hence, the correct answer is "77".**

questions.question: The demand curve is elastic when _______ and it is inelastic when __________.

options.text: marginal revenue has a negative value; average revenue has a positive value

marginal revenue has a positive value; marginal revenue has a negative value
average revenue has a positive value; marginal revenue has a negative value

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **marginal revenue has a positive value; marginal revenue has a negative value**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The **demand curve **is a concept in economics that plots the price of a product or service against how much of the product or service people buy.
 
• Typically, the **lower the price** of an item, the **more people buy**.
 
• However, that relationship varies depending on the item.
 
• An** elastic demand curve means** that a change in price has a large effect on buying, while an inelastic demand curve means that a price change has less effect on buying.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal revenue** is related to the price elasticity of demand — the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price.
 
• When marginal revenue is positive, **demand is elastic**; and when marginal revenue is negative,** demand is inelastic**.
 
• On a graph with both a demand curve and a marginal revenue curve, demand will be elastic at all quantities where **marginal revenue is positive**.
 
• Demand is unit elastic at the quantity where marginal **revenue is zero**. 
 
• If the elasticity of demand is less than zero then it denotes that the change in quantity demand is opposite to the change in its** own price**.
 
• It means that the slope of the demand curve is negative at this point and the marginal revenue is also **negative due to negative slope**.

questions.question: Let x be the median of the data: 16, 78, 26, 91, 29, 71, 31, 46, 9, 51, 54, 56, 61, 21, 62, 65, 73, 86, 41, 89. Let y be the median of the data obtained when 26 and 41 are replaced by 59 and 75, respectively, in the above data. What is the value of (3x - 2y)?

The data: 16, 78, 26, 91, 29, 71, 31, 46, 9, 51, 54, 56, 61, 21, 62, 65, 73, 86, 41, 89

**Formula Used:**

Median for even no. of observations = Average of (n/2)th & (n/2 + 1)/2th term

**Calculations:**

Let the Median of original data be 'x'

Arranging the data in ascending order,

9, 16, 21, 26, 29, 31, 41, 46, 51, 54, 56, 61, 62, 65, 71, 73, 78, 86, 89, 91

⇒ Total no. of observations = 20

⇒ Median = 20/2th + (20/2 + 1)/2th = 10th & 11th term

questions.question: Which of the following institutions has/have the power to issue a writ of 'Habeas corpus' as per the Constitution of India?

options.text: The Supreme Court and the High Court

__

• It is the order issued by the court to present the detenu before the court and to check whether the arrest was lawful or not.
 
• The supreme court under Article 32 and the high court under Article 226 have the power to issue writs of 'Habeas corpus'.
 
• Though under Article 32 the supreme courts issue the writs if there is any violation of the fundamental rights of a person but the High Court under Article 226 has a wider jurisdiction to issue the writ for both a violation of the legal as well as the fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The concept of the writs is to enable the immediate determination of the rights of an individual and help the person to achieve the benefit of his right.
 
• There are five types of writs in our constitution those are as follows:
 
 
• Writ of habeas corpus
 
• Writ of Mandamus
 
• Writ of prohibition
 
• Writ of certiorari
 
• Writ of quo warranto
 
 
 
• The writ of mandamus is the order or command issued by any statute or any authority sanctioned by law to any person, corporation or any other authority in order to perform any public duty.
 
• The writ of prohibition means is a writ issued by the higher authority to its subordinate authority in order to stop something which the law prohibits.
 
• This writ can only be issued against a judicial and quasi-judicial body.
 
• The term certiorari is a Latin word that means to be informed.
 
• This writ is issued by the higher court to review the actions of the lower court.
 
• Writ of quo warranto means by what authority.
 
• This writ is issued which requires a person to show by what authority he has exercised his powers or rights.

questions.question: The L.C.M. of two numbers is 252 and their H.C.F. is 14. If one of the numbers is 28, then by what percentage is the other number more than 28?
questions.solution:

LCM = 252

HCF = 14

One Number = 28

**Formula used:**

Percentage = Required Value/Total Value × 100

**Concept used:**

LCM × HCF = Product of the two numbers

**Calculations:**

Let the other no. be 'a'

⇒ 252 × 14 = 28 × a

⇒ a = (252 × 14)/28

⇒ a = 3528/28 = 126

Required % = (126 - 28)/28 × 100 = (98 × 100)/28 = 350%

**∴ 350% percentage is the other number more than 28.**
